explanation: Pointing at a person or object with the index finger is considered impolite and overly blunt in Indonesia, particularly in traditional Javanese custom. The widely used polite alternative is to point with the thumb, making a relaxed fist and extending the thumb toward the direction or object, or to gesture with an open hand. This matters most when addressing elders or people of higher status.
local_tip: Point with your thumb or an open hand instead of your index finger, especially around elders or in more formal settings.

also_check.note: Index-finger pointing is impolite; an open hand or a nod is used instead.
Index-finger pointing is common and casual, though it can read as blunt in formal settings.
Pointing with the index finger is impolite; people often use their chin or an open hand instead.

sources.title: A Thumb Points the Way in Java
